round3-brief.text:
ROUND 3 — finishing the wallet. One batch, please review it all at once.

NEW: M11 Transaction (tap any history row; fee bump lives here now, so a stuck send is fixable from a phone) · M12 Public keys (xpub + descriptors, for a watch-only copy elsewhere) · M8b Send in Max state (Max now asks the core to drain, so the amount shown is exactly what leaves).

UPDATED: M2 Key gains Watch-only · M5 Unlock gets the two-step Forget the phone was missing · M6 Wallet rows are tappable and show pending sats · M7 Receive can request an amount (QR becomes a bitcoin: link) · M8 Send shows inline errors and a Custom fee rate · M10 Settings rows open Setup (after a 'this closes the wallet' confirm, same block as Forget), plus Rescan and Export.

Desktop: 3 Wallet gets a receive QR + amount, click-to-expand tx detail with the bump inside, a Public keys card and Rescan; 4 Send shows Max state; 2 Key gains Watch-only.

Nothing else moved. Same tokens throughout.

round3-tx-note.text:
M11 — what the row knows

Everything comes from the wallet's own view of the tx: fee and rate (null when an input is not ours, then the row just omits them), which outputs are ours (Change), confirmations from the local tip.

Bump card appears only for an unconfirmed OUTGOING tx. Rate is prefilled from the 1-block estimate; the node rejects a bump below the replacement minimum and we show its wording.

round3-export-note.text:
M12 — public, not secret

The xpub and descriptors let another wallet follow this one (balance, history, receiving) without being able to spend. They do reveal the whole address history, hence the lede.

Single-key wallets show one descriptor and no xpub.

round3-max-note.text:
M8b — Max is a mode, not a number

Tapping Max needs the address first (the exact size depends on it), then asks the core to build a drain: the amount field fills with what actually leaves and Review's Change is 0. Editing the amount drops out of Max. Same on desktop 4.

round3-mobile-updates.text:
Round 3 changes to existing phone boards

M5 Unlock — the red card is what appears after tapping Forget this wallet (the button sits where the card is). Delete it / Keep it, like Settings already does.

M6 Wallet — hero is total incl. pending (matches desktop now; the two disagreed). Rows open M11.

M7 Receive — Copy + New address (Share was never built). Amount is optional.

M8 Send — errors inline under the field, wording shared with desktop. Custom fee chip reveals a sat/vB field.

M10 Settings — Network / Esplora / Address type rows open a confirm ('Changing this closes the wallet') then Setup. Unit and Show-phrase rows removed: neither exists.

round3-desktop-note.text:
Round 3 on desktop 3 · Wallet

Receive card: QR beside the address, optional amount → bitcoin: link.

Transactions: click a row to expand it in place (first row shown open). Bump fee moved into the expansion.

Public keys card + Rescan (gap 20 / 100 / 500) at the bottom — moved to 6 · Settings in Round 6. Rescan exists because a restored wallet that used more than 20 addresses in a row shows too little until it looks further.

hd-note.text:
Roadmap 6 - HD wallet

Key screen becomes a choice: New wallet (BIP39 phrase), Restore wallet, or Advanced: single key (what the app does today).

New wallet shows the 12 words once, then makes you fill three back in before it will continue. Restore validates each word against the BIP39 list and can take an optional passphrase.

Once HD, the dashboard's receive address is the next UNUSED one and change goes to a separate internal keychain.

bump-note.text:
Roadmap 7 + 8

History: an unconfirmed OUTGOING row gets a "Bump fee" button (BDK signals RBF on everything we build). Confirmed and incoming rows show nothing.

Send: amount takes sat or BTC via the unit chips; "Max" fills the spendable balance minus fee. An address that fails validation turns the field red with the reason underneath, and Review stays disabled.

history-note.text:
Roadmap item 4 — Transaction history

New "Transactions" card under Coins: direction arrow (in = green, down; out = up), short txid, signed net amount (sent amounts include the fee), confirmations, relative/short date. Newest first. Click a row → explorer (later).

unlock-note.text:
Keystore flow (roadmap item 1)

Key screen gains "Remember on this device" (OS keychain).
On later launches the app opens on Unlock instead of Key when a wallet is remembered.
Unlock → Wallet. "Use a different wallet" → Key screen. "Forget this wallet" removes the keychain entry after a confirm.

brief.text:
Warm-minimal refinement of the current app tokens.
Same palette (#FAFAF9 / #1A1A1A / accent #C2410C), 4px radius, 34px controls.
Type: IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono (tabular numerals for sats).
Addresses/txids are sample values.

mobile-brief.text:
MOBILE — iOS + Android (Tauri). 390x844 frames.

Same palette and type as the desktop boards; everything else re-scaled for a thumb: 48px controls, 16px input text (anything smaller makes iOS zoom the page on focus), 12px card radius, 999px chips. Status bar, tab bar and home indicator are drawn in so the real usable height is visible.

Home is a balance card over a transaction list, with a fixed bottom tab bar — Wallet / Scan / Settings. Send and Receive are the two buttons under the balance, not tabs, because they are actions rather than places.

These are ADDITIVE: no desktop screen changes. Labels stay English to match the rest of the app.

Things worth arguing about before I build it:
- Wallet / Scan / Settings as the three tabs, or drop Scan into the Send screen and make the third tab something else?
- M6: BTC as the big number with sats underneath, or the reverse?
- M3: 12 words in two columns fits without scrolling; a 24-word restore will scroll. OK?
- M9 Scan is the only dark screen. Deliberate (camera), or make it light?

mobile-native-note.text:
What each mobile-only affordance costs

M7 Receive QR — pure JS, no native plugin.
M9 Scan — tauri-plugin-barcode-scanner, camera permission string in Info.plist and AndroidManifest.
M5 Unlock — tauri-plugin-biometric; it authenticates, it does not hold the key, so the key still sits in iOS Keychain / Android Keystore and Face ID gates the read.
M8 Send also opens from a bitcoin: deep link (tauri-plugin-deep-link), prefilled.

M10 'Show recovery phrase' is behind the same biometric gate.

round6-brief.text:
ROUND 6 — product. Reviewed on 2026-09-30.

NEW phone: Unlock with reset, Send to several, Coins, Speed up, Cancel, Import PSBT, focus rings, Settings with Lock/Coins/Import.
NEW desktop: Settings, Unlock and Remember with an app password (browser build), Coins, Speed up/Cancel, Import PSBT.

Decided:
(1) Reset only when the saved data cannot be read. Data saved by a newer app version asks for an update instead, since a reset would lose what that version keeps.
(2) Lock after 5 minutes in the background by default. A wallet that is not remembered stays open.
(3) App password: PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 rounds and AES-GCM, named 'App password'.
(4) Several recipients: one unit for all rows; scanning fills the last empty row.
(5) Rescan and Public keys move to Settings; 3 · Wallet keeps neither.

round6-settings-note.text:
6 · Settings (6.8, 6.11)

Opened from the gear in the top bar. 3 · Wallet is changed in place for it: the gear is its only change, and 3b, 3c and 7 carry the same gear. Chain rows ask first, then close the wallet and open Setup, as on the phone. Lock after is the phone's setting too. Import PSBT gets a card here, as it gets a row on the phone.

Forget is drawn open at its second step. Rescan and Public keys live here only: 3 · Wallet gave them up — choice (5).

round6-unlock-pw-note.text:
2e · Unlock with an app password (6.12, browser build only)

The browser has no keychain, so a remembered key is encrypted with an 'App password' (WebCrypto, AES-GCM) and kept in IndexedDB. It is not the BIP39 passphrase: that one is part of the wallet, this one only locks the copy in this browser.

A wrong password is its own error, under the field. The desktop app keeps the Keychain (2b) and asks for no password.

round6-remember-note.text:
2f · Remember with an app password (6.12)

In the browser build, ticking Remember on this device reveals App password and Confirm app password; Open wallet waits until they match. Nothing is stored without them. Key derivation and the name are choice (3).

Create and Restore get the same two fields under their Remember box, right below the BIP39 passphrase — which is why the name must differ.

round6-coins-desktop-note.text:
3b · Coins on the desktop (6.13)

The Coins card on 3 · Wallet gains a checkbox and a Frozen switch per row. A frozen row is dimmed and cannot be ticked. Send selected opens 4 · Send held to the ticked coins; with none ticked it is hidden and sends choose coins on their own, as today.

round6-txactions-note.text:
3c · Speed up and Cancel on the desktop (6.14)

The rows of 3 · Wallet, which open one at a time; both unconfirmed rows are drawn open here. An unconfirmed incoming row offers Speed up, previewed before signing. An unconfirmed outgoing row keeps Bump fee and adds Cancel, which asks first with the same card as M11c. Confirmed rows offer neither.

round6-psbt-desktop-note.text:
7 · Import PSBT (6.15)

From Settings. Paste it or load a file; it is described as soon as it parses: inputs (ours or not, signed or not), outputs, fee. Sign signs the inputs this wallet holds keys for. Broadcast stays disabled until the PSBT is finalized.

round6-unlock-reset-note.text:
M5b — reset history, keep the key (6.7)

When the key opens but this device's saved history cannot be read (corrupt_state), Unlock says so and offers a reset. It deletes only that wallet's history here and opens the wallet again; the next sync downloads it back. The key and the settings stay.

The lower card is the second step, as with Forget. Key, Restore and Create show the same error with the same reset.

round6-settings-phone-note.text:
M10b — Settings, three new rows

Lock after (6.11): how long the app may sit in the background before a remembered wallet closes to Unlock, never mid-sync or mid-broadcast. 5 min is the proposed default — choice (2).

Coins (M13) and Import PSBT (M14) open their own screens.

It no longer fits one screen, so it scrolls: Close wallet, Forget and the wallet id sit below, unchanged.

round6-send-multi-note.text:
M8c — Send to several (6.9)

Each recipient is a card: address, scan, amount, and × to remove it (hidden while only one is left). One sat/BTC choice covers every row, and scanning fills the last empty row — choice (4).

Max is not shown: it exists only with a single recipient, as on desktop 4. Review lists every recipient, then fee and total.

round6-coins-note.text:
M13 — Coins (6.13)

From Settings → Coins. Every unspent output, with its outpoint and confirmations. Tick coins to spend only those; the switch freezes one. A frozen coin is dimmed, cannot be ticked, and stays out of automatic selection, Max and the spendable balance until unfrozen. Freezing is saved with the wallet.

Send selected opens Send held to the ticked coins.

round6-psbt-note.text:
M14 — Import PSBT (6.15)

From Settings → Import PSBT. Paste it, or scan it when it fits one QR code (animated QR stays under Later). It is described before anything is signed: which inputs are ours, where each output goes, the fee.

Sign signs the inputs this wallet holds keys for. Broadcast stays disabled until every input is signed and the PSBT is finalized. A watch-only wallet has no Sign but can broadcast a PSBT signed elsewhere.

round6-speedup-note.text:
M11b — Speed up an incoming payment (6.14)

Only on an unconfirmed INCOMING transaction. It spends the payment on to this wallet with a fee big enough that the two together reach the chosen rate (CPFP). The fee comes out of the payment: 28,886 of the 30,000 sat arrive.

The action card sits above the Transaction id card (one scroll down), so it shows without scrolling. M11's Bump card can move up the same way.

round6-cancel-note.text:
M11c — Cancel an outgoing payment (6.14)

Only while it is unconfirmed, and only if the original signalled RBF — every transaction this wallet builds does. The replacement pays everything back to this wallet at a fee that meets BIP125's absolute-fee rule, not only the rate. Two steps, like Forget.

Bump fee folds away while Cancel is open. If the original confirms first, the cancel is rejected and the payment stands.

round6-focus-note.text:
M15 — Focus rings (6.10)

Keyboard focus only (:focus-visible); a tap draws nothing. Rows and tabs take a 2px #C2410C ring inside their edge, since the card and the tab bar would clip one outside. The primary button takes a 2px #1A1A1A ring 2px outside: an orange ring vanishes against the orange fill. Fields and textareas get the ring desktop inputs already have.
